_comment: VD.1 — verify_deliberate_break_is_detected. The RECORDED OUTCOME of a real
deliberate-break round, so the verification is re-gradeable rather than
asserted in prose:  node tools/capture/break-check.mjs --grade reviews/break-round-debug-affordance.json
Method. `break-check.mjs --break debug-affordance` removed the Debug
affordance card from client/src/pages/tx.nim (24 lines: the button, its
availability badge, its explanatory note and the per-execution list), rebuilt
the site with the static exporter, captured tx-detail at wide/light into
screenshots/break/debug-affordance/, and restored the source. Six disposable
sub-agents were then given the prompts `review-prompt.mjs` generates — byte
identical to a normal review round. None was told that anything had been
removed, or that this was a test.
The `reviews` array below holds their ledger blocks verbatim, trimmed only in
`findings` to the first finding of each (which is what the grading examines)
plus a count of what followed. The full reports are summarised in `_report`.
The `control` array records the SAME prompts run against the UNBROKEN capture
screenshots/tx-detail__wide__light.png. Without it, 'every reviewer said the
Debug button was missing' would not be evidence that the expectation block
detects the break: a block strict enough to fail every capture would score
identically. The control reviewers located the element on the page and
described where it was, which is what makes the broken round's 'it does not
exist anywhere on the page' a discrimination rather than a reflex.

findings.location: hero, right of the "Transaction" H1 and status chip
findings.finding: No Debug button exists anywhere on the page. The strongest control the design requires is absent, so the hero terminates at the H1 and the eye falls straight into the overview grid; there is no hero -> Debug -> overview path to read.

reviews._report: Led with the missing Debug button, then two further P1s (hero age/finality/copy affordance; the trace line stranded with no Debug action beside it) and six P2/P3 typography findings — section eyebrows weaker than the grid labels they head, the monospace face spent on labels rather than values, a raw `feePayer` field name in a Capitalised label set.

findings.location: hero, band between the full hash line and the OVERVIEW section rule
findings.finding: The Debug button is absent from the hero. The page's primary action — the one affordance that distinguishes this product from every other explorer, and which brief §1 rule 1 requires to be primary wherever a transaction appears — does not exist on the transaction page. Its absence also strands the required 'Internal calls and state changes come from the execution trace.' line in the events/internal-calls/state-changes panel with no Debug action beside it to request that trace, and removes the trace-availability state and its worded note entirely.

reviews._report: Obeyed the single-finding constraint exactly: one element, one location, one reason, one severity, and named the missing Debug button as 'the weakest element because it is not weak — it is not there'.

control.controlNote: Located the Debug affordance ON the unbroken page — 'the primary button in the hero trace-availability panel, immediately left of the orange onDemand badge', labelled 'Generate trace'. It reported the element as REPLACED (present but unrecognisable: near-white label on a near-white fill, ~1:1 contrast) rather than MISSING, and gave its position. That is the discrimination the verification needs: the same reviewer role, the same prompt, the same expectation block — element found and located when present, reported as existing nowhere on the page when removed.
control.verbatimFinding: The page's primary action renders as an unlabelled white slab: the button fill is near-white and its 'Generate trace' label is also near-white, giving effectively zero contrast, so the single strongest control on the most important page in the product cannot be read at 100%.

control.controlNote: Also failed the presence check on the unbroken page — but for OTHER elements (hero copy affordance, age, finality badge, overview value/nonce/type, events section, receipt JSON), and its `missing` list does NOT contain the Debug button. It located the control by coordinate instead: 'the Generate trace button at x405-540'. So the reviewer that reports ten missing items on the unbroken page still does not report this one, and does report it first on the broken one. That is the discrimination, measured against a reviewer that was already in a failing mood.
control.verbatimFinding: The primary control compounds it: the 'Generate trace' button at x405-540 is near-white text on a near-white pill and reads as a blank shape at 100%.

_productFindingsSurfaced: The unbroken tx-detail page's PRIMARY BUTTON IS UNREADABLE: a near-white 'Generate trace' label on a near-white fill, ~1:1 contrast, on a near-black canvas. Found by the control review, not by the break. This is a real P1 for VD.2 — a light-theme button surface token landing on a dark-theme page while the label keeps its light foreground.
Independently re-confirmed VD.0's finding that the token layer is dark-only: five of six reviewers noted that the `light` capture renders a near-black canvas.
Internal milestone identifiers (M5/M9, 'WASM replay + ViewModels', 'a later slice') are rendered on the public transaction page's deferred-section notes.
The label column mixes prose labels (Block, Canonical, Finality) with raw adapter field names (feePayer).
